purpose: Docetaxel is used to treat several types of cancer, including breast cancer, lung cancer, prostate cancer, stomach cancer, and head and neck cancer. It is often given when other treatments have not worked or to help shrink tumors before surgery. Your doctor may use it alone or combine it with other cancer medicines.
how_it_works: Think of cancer cells like they are constantly trying to divide and grow out of control. Docetaxel works by interfering with the internal skeleton that cancer cells need to split apart and multiply. By blocking this process, the drug essentially freezes the cancer cells so they cannot reproduce and they eventually die off.
common_side_effects: Low blood counts (which can increase your risk of infection, fatigue, or bruising), hair loss, mouth sores, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, swelling in your hands or feet (fluid retention), numbness or tingling in your hands and feet, nail changes, and feeling very tired.
warnings: Docetaxel can seriously lower your immune system, making it easier to get life-threatening infections — call your doctor right away if you have a fever. It can cause severe allergic reactions, especially during the infusion, so you will be given steroids beforehand to help prevent this. It may also cause liver problems, and your doctor will regularly check your blood counts and liver function. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, bleeding, severe swelling, trouble breathing, or signs of infection. This medication can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is essential during treatment.
typical_dosing: Docetaxel is given through an IV (directly into your vein) at a cancer clinic or hospital, usually once every 3 weeks. Each infusion typically takes about 1 hour. The exact dose your doctor prescribes depends on your body size, the type of cancer being treated, and how well you are tolerating the medicine. You will be given steroid pills to take for a couple of days before each infusion to reduce the chance of a serious allergic reaction and fluid buildup.
